nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Multivariable fractional polynomial regression (mfp package in R) used for normative models.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Leveraging the CentileBrain pipeline, we opted for multivariable fractional polynomial regression implemented with the mfp package in R.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional subcortical volume, cortical thickness, and surface area.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We have developed sex-specific normative models on regional subcortical volume, cortical thickness, and surface area data from 457 healthy children sourced from two datasets.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Covariates included age, sex, site (random factor with ComBat-GAM harmonization), and global measures (ICV, mean cortical thickness, mean surface area) depending on regional model.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Using age and sex as covariates, normative models for each regional morphometric measure were developed utilizing data from a multisite sample of 457 healthy individuals (47.3% female; aged 3 to 18 years) from the devCCNP. The two samples were combined to train the normative models, and the potential impact of site on performance is addressed by treating site as a random factor and using ComBatGAM (Pomponio et al. 2020) for site harmonization. The optimal covariate combination included site harmonization (ComBat-GAM) ( Pomponio et al. 2020) and the incorporation of intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, and mean surface area in the regional models for subcortical volume, cortical thickness, and surface area regional measures, respectively.
